introduction: We develop learning and control methods that help embodied agents understand human intent, learn physical dynamics, and act reliably under uncertainty.

themes.title: Learning Physical Dynamics
themes.question: How can we learn how physical systems evolve from imperfect observations?
themes.description: Physical systems are shaped by uncertainty, history, and interactions that can be difficult to capture with a fixed model. We study data-driven representations of dynamical systems, including signature methods and Koopman learning, to model their evolution from noisy or partially observed trajectories. This work builds foundations for prediction and control in physical AI.

themes.title: Human-Guided Learning and Decision-Making
themes.question: How can an agent understand what people want and act with incomplete information?
themes.description: An intelligent agent must learn the task as well as the environment. We investigate how human preferences can teach complex temporal behaviors without requiring explicit logical specifications, and how agents can plan perception-related tasks under partial observability. Our work connects human feedback, task representations, and decision-making under uncertainty.

themes.title: Reliable Planning and Control
themes.question: How can learning agents accomplish complex tasks while respecting safety constraints?
themes.description: We combine reinforcement learning, formal task specifications, and control theory to develop policies with explicit guarantees. Our research addresses constrained planning, convergence of model-free learning, and the mathematical foundations of temporal-logic objectives. These methods support reliable decisions when tasks extend over time and objectives must be balanced against safety requirements.
